case_studies.title: Learning Safe Agent Behaviour from Human Preferences and Justifications via World Models
case_studies.abstract: We address the problem of safely training an agent policy and deploying a good and safe policy, in settings where the environment dynamics are unknown and no suitable reward function is available. In the context of safety-critical environments, we consider traditional reinforcement learning impractical and resort to the resource of human input. We introduce DROPJ, a human-centred method for both safe training and deployment. We first learn a world model (a learned simulator) from a dataset of prior real-world trajectories. A human then plays the game in this learned simulator to extract severa
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of safely training an agent policy in unknown environments, it built a human-centred method called DROPJ, and the result is a safer deployment of agent policies. The method uses human input and a learned world model to achieve this. This research is not directly relevant to managing cloud infrastructure.

case_studies.title: SAFETY SENTRY: Context-Aware Human Intervention via EXECUTE-ASK-REFUSE Routing
case_studies.abstract: LLM agents act on real-world environments through tool calls, and a single misjudged action can cause irreversible harm. The standard safeguard is a guard model that labels each proposed action as safe or unsafe, but this binary view conflates two distinct decisions: whether the action is harmful in itself, and whether it is appropriate given the user's context. It also operates at the granularity of action categories rather than individual instances, producing routine interruptions that erode autonomy and train users to wave through the most consequential alerts. We reframe the problem as a p
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of preventing harmful actions by AI agents in real-world environments by introducing a more nuanced approach to human intervention. The researchers built a system called SAFETY SENTRY, which routes proposed actions through an execute-ask-refuse process. The result is a more context-aware and autonomous system that reduces unnecessary interruptions.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage AI-powered systems that interact with the physical world, consider implementing a similar context-aware intervention system to reduce the risk of harmful actions. Check your current guard models to see if they conflate safety and appropriateness decisions. This may require adjustments to your system's decision-making architecture and alerting mechanisms.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novelty: LLM agents and safety concerns are novel, but the concept of executing actions in real-world environments is not. IT Relevance: Directly affects how AI interacts with real-world environments, but the problem is more about AI development than IT deployment. Value: LLM agents interacting with real-world environments can cause harm, and the proposed 'EXECUTE-ASK-REFUSE Routing' could potentially mitigate this in an IT infrastructure context.

case_studies.title: Grokipedia vs Wikipedia: An LLM-Based Audit of Political Neutrality along Ideologies
case_studies.abstract: Online encyclopedias shape political opinion and, through it, democratic discourse. In late 2025, Grokipedia was released, an encyclopedia written entirely by the LLM Grok. One motivation behind the project was to provide an unbiased alternative to Wikipedia, which has faced accusations of "left-wing" and "liberal" bias. But does an encyclopedia written by an LLM deliver greater neutrality, or does it simply embed a different ideology? We conduct a large-scale political bias study on Grokipedia and Wikipedia, analysing 1,394 article pairs describing members of government for neutrality along n
case_studies.summary: This research compares the political neutrality of Grokipedia, an online encyclopedia written by a large language model, with Wikipedia, finding whether one is more unbiased than the other. The researchers built a large-scale study analyzing article pairs from both sites. The result shows how each encyclopedia presents political information, but it's not directly relevant to managing cloud infrastructure.

case_studies.abstract: Humanoid control requires natural whole-body coordination, precise real-time responses to control signals, and robust generalization across diverse environmental contexts, making it a cornerstone for generalist embodied agents. Behavior Foundation Models (BFMs) have recently emerged as a promising solution to address these challenges by leveraging large-scale behavioral data to achieve superior expressiveness, versatility and generalization. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of controlling humanoid robots by building Behavior Foundation Models that can learn from large-scale behavioral data, resulting in improved expressiveness, versatility, and generalization. The researchers investigated how to scale these models for better capabilities. This research is not directly relevant to managing cloud infrastructure.

case_studies.title: Copy-on-Write Scoring: Application-Specific Agent Evaluations
case_studies.abstract: Trustworthy deployment of LLM-based agents in software systems requires evaluating how they perform on application-specific workflows, with enough granularity to localize where they succeed and fail. Yet existing agent evaluation mechanisms are limited: benchmarks have low construct validity for application-specific workflows and environments, and replica evaluation environments are expensive and prone to drift. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of evaluating the performance of Large Language Model (LLM)-based agents in specific software systems. The authors built a framework called Copy-on-Write Scoring to assess agent operations directly within application environments. The result is a more accurate evaluation of agent performance in real-world workflows.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage LLM-based agents in software systems, here is what to do: assess your current evaluation mechanisms, consider implementing Copy-on-Write Scoring for more accurate results, and review your PostgreSQL configuration to support this framework. This flags a risk: if your organization uses LLM-based agents, check your evaluation processes to ensure they are effective and reliable. Not directly applicable to general IT infrastructure work, but relevant to those managing LLM-based systems.
case_studies.score_reasoning: The paper introduces a novel framework for evaluating LLM-based agents within application environments, which could be relevant for IT engineers working with software systems and LLM APIs. case_studies.title: CAVA: Canonical Action Verification and Attestation for Runtime Governance of Agentic AI Systems
case_studies.abstract: Agentic AI systems increasingly act through heterogeneous runtimes: local coding hooks, SDK tools, browser automation, managed-agent traces, API gateways, and workflow engines. A single operational act such as publishing code, changing identity state, moving money, or exporting data may therefore be represented by many incompatible runtime records. This makes a basic governance question difficult to answer: what action was actually approved, what evidence binds the approval to execution, and can an independent verifier reproduce the same action identity later? This paper presents Canonical Act
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of verifying actions in AI systems that use multiple runtimes, by creating a system called CAVA that can provide a single, reliable record of what actions were taken. The result is a more trustworthy and auditable AI system. This is relevant to IT work in managing AI and cloud infrastructure.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage AI systems or cloud infrastructure that uses multiple runtimes, here is what to do: review your current governance and auditing processes, consider implementing a system like CAVA to provide a single record of actions, and check your compliance with relevant regulations. This flags a risk: if your org uses AI systems with multiple runtimes, check your auditing and logging processes immediately to ensure you can verify actions taken. Not directly applicable to non-AI or non-cloud IT infrastructure work.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novelty: Uncovering the challenges of agentic AI systems' runtime governance. Novel ideas on how AI actions could be verified and attested. IT Relevance: Directly affects how IT engineers work with agentic systems and their governance. Value 90 days: Practical ideas could be implemented within 90 days to automate action verification.
